axis: haste as plain fast movement → haste that turns careless and costs the mover dignity

members.tone: The plainest name for going fast and going badly at once, with the carelessness carried quietly rather than pressed.
Puts the weight on momentum - a harder-edged, more headlong version of *hurry*, where the speed is what overrides the care.
Formal and weighty, naming the hurry as a fault to be answered for where *hurry* merely reports it.
The participle keeps the careless speed running on as an activity rather than a single lapse, unlike the finished act *rush* names.
Great speed as a sudden break away, all abruptness and no blame - the carelessness that shadows *hurry* is absent.
Speed as a short spirited burst, brisk and deliberate beside the startled suddenness of *bolt*.
Makes the hurry small and skittering, so the loss of dignity comes out as comic rather than damning.
The undignified hurry as graceless floundering - effortful disorder where *scamper* is merely quick and silly.
